blocks.text: This is the SSO sign-in prototype from `sso-client-scoping/components/login-journey`, carried into a living document as a sample of the migration. The screen is the real one — type an address and it answers. What changed is who owns the words on it: every string is now yours to edit, and the seven comment threads that sat open on the published copy become typed operations the journal can read back.

blocks.text: Three of the seven were the single word *drop*. On a plain artefact each one is a thread a human has to open, read the anchor of, and act on. Here a delete is a gesture and the journal carries what left. The other four were a copy change, a structural request, a standing rule and a hand-off to another document — which is one string edit, one note, one style directive and one tag.

blocks.info: The three steps, so the real one in sso-client-scoping is a repeat and not a redesign.

items: **Make every string an element.** The original built its dynamic text with `innerHTML` strings — `'Sending you to ' + customer + '…'`. Those cannot be marked. Each became an element with `data-la-text`, and the customer name a separate `<span>` the script fills. The logic did not change; it now toggles `hidden` instead of rebuilding markup.
**List the strings in `labels` under the same keys.** The build refuses a label with no element behind it, so a typo is caught before publishing, not after.

**Carry the open threads over as what they are.** A copy request is an edit or a note. A rule is a style directive. A *drop* is a delete. A hand-off to another document is a `seed-next` tag. Nothing is pasted as a comment.

blocks.title: Not done here, on purpose
blocks.text: The real prototype still lives in `sso-client-scoping`, and its seven threads stay open on the old artefact because none was sent to Claude — they cannot be resolved from a session. Migrating it for real is: this same screen file into that repo's `docs/`, the threads applied against the real plan, and the old artefact's record pointed at the new URL.
